title: How the ZIA Terraform provider applies rule order

prose.text: The ZIA provider does not write a rule's order directly. It moves the rule out of the way first and puts it back later, in the background. {{update-parks-every-update}} {{list-error-then-panic}} {{parking-spot-from-truncated-list}}

prose.label: Rules the apply did not touch.
prose.text: {{terminal-rule-can-be-displaced}} Product-side rule order semantics are in [[zia.url-filtering.rule-order]].

checks.do: Whether the terminal rules are still last after an apply that edited ordered rules, by re-reading the whole policy's order rather than only the edited rules.
Whether a later plan shows rules out of their declared order after an apply that reported success.

update-parks-every-update.statement: Every URL Filtering rule update, whatever field changed, is first sent with rank 7 at the order of the last rule (sorted by rank, then order), and only afterwards moved back to its declared order by the reorder worker. The rule is written at that order, not after it.

list-error-then-panic.statement: Before v4.8.11, if listing the existing rules failed during an update, the error was only logged and the code read the last element of whatever came back: if the first page failed, the list was empty and the index panicked; if a later page failed, the rule was parked using a partial list. v4.8.11 returns the list error from the update before the index is read (#610).

parking-spot-from-truncated-list.statement: The parking order comes from a list read through the Go SDK's GetAll, which can return a truncated list. With more rules than one page holds, the "highest existing order" can be a position inside the policy rather than its end.

background-worker.statement: Declared orders are applied by one background worker per rule type. It rescans on a 30-second ticker, sleeping for half the interval between checks, and each pass reads current positions once.

worker-cannot-report-failure.statement: The reorder worker has no way to report failure: `reorderAll` returns no value, and waiting resources are released by closing a channel. A reorder that gives up looks like success to Terraform.

upstream.note: Filing 2 (reorder redesign): partial completion must return an error.

converges-on-registered-rules-only.statement: A pass is judged only on the rules registered by this apply: it is "clean" when none of them needed a move, was skipped, or failed. Rules the apply did not touch, including a terminal deny, are never checked.

quotes: cleanPass := putsIssued == 0 && skipped == 0 && puterrs == 0 && size == lastSize

stale-positions-within-a-pass.statement: Within a pass, each rule is compared against the positions read at the start of the pass; positions are not refreshed after a move, so later rules in the same pass are judged against stale positions.

gives-up-silently.statement: The worker returns without an error in several situations: after six ticks in which registered rules stay deferred or their moves fail with no progress, or after two ticks in which only deferred rules remain. From v4.8.7 an oscillation breaker also returns after repeated non-improving passes (SUP-4231). From v4.8.11 it also returns after six consecutive passes in which the current rule order could not be read (#610); before v4.8.11 a failed read only logged the error and continued, so a read that kept failing kept the worker looping. Waiters proceed as if the order were applied; the v4.8.11 comment says the waiting create or update then reads the rule back and reports the API error.

wrong-order-reported-success.statement: So an apply can finish successfully with rules out of their declared order, and only a later plan's drift shows it.

terminal-rule-can-be-displaced.statement: Editing any field of a rule placed above a terminal deny can leave the deny no longer last: the edit parks the rule below it, and if moving it back fails or gives up, the apply still reports success.
terminal-rule-can-be-displaced.conditions: Depends on how the API renumbers the other rules when one is written at a given order, and on the API accepting a write at the last rule's order even when that is a predefined default rule (gap api-order-shift); on the edited rule not already being last and the terminal rule being at or near the end; and on the move back failing or giving up.

api-order-shift.title: How the ZIA API renumbers other rules when a rule is written at a given order
api-order-shift.blocks: stating exactly where a parked rule lands and which neighbors move
api-order-shift.detail: The provider assumes ordered-list behavior (the written rule takes the position and the rest shift). No captured source states the API's renumbering rule, or whether it rejects a write at a predefined default rule's order. Test in a scratch tenant by writing a rule at a lower order, and at the default rule's order, and re-reading every rule's order.
